key_insight: The paper proves that Barzilai--Borwein (BB1) is not superlinearly convergent on a nonempty open set of strictly convex quadratic problems in every dimension n≥4.
engineering_relevance: This warns practitioners that BB1 can be fast in practice yet still exhibit only geometric convergence on certain quadratic problems, so relying on superlinear behavior is unsafe.
method: Constructs an open family of strictly convex quadratics and initial points with bad BB dynamics
Uses a computer-assisted proof of an attracting nonresonant seven-cycle in the projectivized BB system
Derives two-sided geometric bounds for gradient, error, and objective gap
evidence_signal: The abstract reports explicit constants (ρ_min=10^-6, ρ_max=0.61) and geometric lower/upper bounds showing convergence but ruling out root-superlinear rates.
watch_item: The result is for a constructed open set of quadratic instances with a computer-assisted proof, so it does not claim typical failure for all problems or all BB variants.
paper_title: Barzilai-Borwein Fails Superlinear Convergence on an Open Set of Quadratics for Every Dimension $n\geq 4$
